pr_title: Force multiple of 4 sizes for Betsy compressor.
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/104260

Padding code copied for existing `_compress_etcpak()`.
pr_comments: I'm pretty sure padding isn't necessary here, simply rounding the compressed image's resolution to the nearest multiple of 4 should work

> simply rounding the compressed image's resolution to the nearest multiple of 4 should work

Would it result it the image resampling (and loss of sharpness as the result) in this case, or am I missing something.

> Would it result it the image resampling (and loss of sharpness as the result) in this case, or am I missing something.

It shouldn't, the sampler is set to clamp at the edges, so the hardware will take care of the padding automatically
Nevermind, it looks like the compute shader skips writing to the "extended" areas, so software padding is probably the way to go

Tested with [v.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19315119/v.zip)

Currently, either half of the texture gets corrupted, or it causes the editor to crash

> Currently, either half of the texture gets corrupted, or it causes the editor to crash

Will fix in a moment, I have used the wrong `width` in one place.

> I can't find where this code actually resizes the source image.

It is not (neither this nor etcpak). It's only adding padding to the raw image data.

> Smear the last 3 pixels on x and y instead of resizing could work, but the user would have to know this was done and adjust all their texture coordinates to (x / x + 3) which is really confusing. The fact that it will subtly break UVs is why I don't think we can do this.

Yes, but this is already the case with software `etcpak` (if you disable GPU compression in settings).
Actually, it looks like this will break for images with formats other than RGBA8

> Actually, it looks like this will break for images with formats other than RGBA8

Indeed, etcpak seems to convert it to RGBA first, not sure if it's what should be added (there are formats with bigger pixel size, so it might be lossy conversion), or it's better to add another loop and smear each pixel component individually.

> Indeed, etcpak seems to convert it to RGBA first, not sure if it's what should be added (there are formats with bigger pixel size, so it might be lossy conversion), or it's better to add another loop and smear each pixel component individually.

This could probably be achieved with `memcpy` and pointer magic
Tested it again, now with almost every uncompressed format. The smearing works as intended now. I'll do more testing and review this later, just to be sure

issue_context.title: Textures black in Godot 4.4 web export
issue_context.body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.4 stable

Non reproducible in 4.3 stable

### System information

Godot v4.4.stable - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - AMD Radeon RX 7900 GRE (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 32.0.12033.1030) - AMD Ryzen 7 7700X 8-Core Processor (16 threads)

### Issue description

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/68556133-58af-43f8-8c4c-dc4e9cbe0fb1)

Textures are black when Godot project is exported to web. I have tried all rendering methods, and have had a friend recreate the issue on his own system. I uploaded to Itch and Newgrounds and it was the same on both platforms. The included Godot robot .svg seems to remain visible though. The issue does not seem to exist on previous Godot version. I have recreated the exact same project on different versions, and only in 4.4 does this issue occur. Exporting to .exe works with no issues.

### Steps to reproduce

Create a scene with an object that you can apply a texture to (mesh, sprite3D). Have a camera view the object. Export and upload to web.


### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[Godot bug MRP.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19278294/Godot.bug.MRP.zip)

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4a01e008-79d1-4f9c-a019-3c5f278be4f0)
example of what the MRP looks like when exported to web
comments:
Tested with Firefox 136.0.1 on macOS, issue is reproducible:

Errors in the console:
```
WebGL warning: compressedTexImage: 250 is never a valid width for level 0, because it implies a base mip width of 250. COMPRESSED_RGBA_S3TC_DXT5_EXT requires that base mip levels have a width multiple of 4.

WebGL warning: compressedTexImage: 125 is never a valid width for level 1, because it implies a base mip width of 250. COMPRESSED_RGBA_S3TC_DXT5_EXT requires that base mip levels have a width multiple of 4.
```

Works fine if tree texture is resized to 256×256 (currently 260×250) and reimported.

For the reference, this is documented limitation for [WEBGL_compressed_texture_s3tc](https://registry.khronos.org/webgl/extensions/WEBGL_compressed_texture_s3tc/):

> width << level and height << level must be a multiple of 4.
The issue seems to be specific to new `BetsyCompressor` (texture compression on GPU), it's not checking the texture size, old software compressor do.

review_comments:
Don't we need to resize the texture as in the etcpak code?
See here:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/4.3/modules/etcpak/image_compress_etcpak.cpp#L169..L173
That was in 4.3, now we only smear: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/28102e6682c7c733a23de461e30d5ae2d33fe755/modules/etcpak/image_compress_etcpak.cpp#L187-L190
